title: Designing Edge-to-Cloud Operational Platforms
topic: Designing edge-to-cloud operational platforms: telemetry, streaming, resilience, vision, and optimization for critical industrial systems

concepts.title: The Operational System Design Problem
concepts.brief: Why industrial and transportation systems differ from ordinary web applications; the characteristics of field operations; the difference between telemetry, commands, decisions, and safety-critical control; the connected rail network running example; design goals.

concepts.title: Requirements Before Architecture
concepts.brief: Turning a vague prompt into measurable requirements; functional and nonfunctional requirements; failure modes as first-class requirements; capacity estimation; producing a system-design specification.

concepts.title: Core Concepts and Tradeoffs
concepts.brief: Control plane vs data plane; hot, warm, and cold paths; event time vs processing time; delivery semantics; idempotency, dedup, replay, reconciliation; consistency; CAP; RPO, RTO, MTTR, error budgets, SLOs.

concepts.title: Designing the Edge Telemetry Agent
concepts.brief: Responsibilities of an on-vehicle agent; hardware and operating constraints; the edge data model; durable local queues and write-ahead logs; store-and-forward; disk exhaustion policies; runtime choice.

concepts.title: Connectivity, Synchronization, and Backpressure
concepts.brief: Connection loss as a normal operating condition; retry strategies; reconnect storms; synchronizing an offline event log; the three acknowledgments; backpressure propagation; QoS classes; dead-letter handling.

concepts.title: Secure Fleet and Device Management
concepts.brief: Device enrollment and provisioning; per-device credentials and certificate rotation; mutual TLS; the identity hierarchy; remote configuration; firmware rollout strategies; command-and-control; digital twins; revocation and threat modeling.

concepts.title: Event Contracts and Schema Evolution
concepts.brief: What makes an event a durable interface; telemetry envelopes; topic taxonomy; Protobuf, Avro, and JSON Schema tradeoffs; schema registry design; compatibility; versioning; field-level governance; data-quality contracts.

concepts.title: Kafka and the Streaming Backbone
concepts.brief: Kafka's mental model; designing topic boundaries; partition-key selection; the ordering-versus-parallelism tradeoff; partition-count planning; replication and durability; retention and compaction; producer and consumer configuration; operational observability.

concepts.title: Rebalancing, Ordering, and Correct Processing
concepts.brief: Why rebalances occur; eager vs cooperative rebalancing; static membership; rebalance-safe consumer design; the poison-pill problem; idempotent consumers; inbox and outbox; deduplication; per-asset ordering; what exactly-once actually means.

concepts.title: Stream Processing and Operational Intelligence
concepts.brief: Choosing a stream processor; stateless and stateful transformations; event-time processing and watermarks; late and missing data; checkpoints and stateful recovery; joins; real-time anomaly detection; alert suppression and escalation; serving live state.

concepts.title: Availability, Consistency, and Graceful Degradation
concepts.brief: Applying CAP without oversimplifying it; classifying services by failure consequence; read-only, cached, delayed, and offline modes; safe fallback states; dependency hierarchies; bulkheads and circuit breakers; degradation examples; human-in-the-loop escalation; runbooks.

concepts.title: Multi-AZ, Multi-Region, and Disaster Recovery
concepts.brief: Zones vs regions; active-active, active-passive, and pilot-light; stateless vs stateful failover; replication strategies; split-brain prevention and fencing; global routing and health checks; cross-region Kafka; RPO/RTO by data class; backup, restore, and DR testing; chaos engineering.

concepts.title: Observability and Operational Forensics
concepts.brief: Observability across edge, network, stream, and cloud; the three pillars and their limits; correlation IDs across boundaries; fleet health dashboards; measuring freshness rather than availability; telemetry metrics; alert design; SLOs; audit trails and forensic replay.

concepts.title: Computer Vision at the Edge
concepts.unit: Part V — Vision and Spatial Data
concepts.brief: Why vision needs a different pipeline than telemetry; camera, drone, and inspection-car sources; edge vs cloud inference; model packaging and hardware acceleration; frame sampling and adaptive upload; detections as events; human review queues; model drift and rollback.

concepts.title: Media Ingestion and Lakehouse Architecture
concepts.unit: Part V — Vision and Spatial Data
concepts.brief: Separating media objects from metadata events; resumable multipart upload; content hashing and dedup; object storage layout; Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers; data lineage; retention classes and tiering; lifecycle policies; table formats and schema evolution; spatial and temporal partitioning.

concepts.title: Spatial Data and Inspection Workflows
concepts.unit: Part V — Vision and Spatial Data
concepts.brief: Coordinates, routes, track segments, mileposts, and linear referencing; mapping telemetry to network topology; spatial indexes; creating an inspection finding; correlating images and sensor readings; the defect lifecycle; confidence and human adjudication; training-data curation.

concepts.title: Modeling Planning and Scheduling Problems
concepts.unit: Part VI — Distributed Scheduling and Optimization
concepts.brief: Optimization vs transactional systems; why schedules are plans, not truth; modeling assets, crews, routes, terminals, and constraints; hard vs soft constraints; objectives; graph representations; solution techniques; decomposing a large problem; uncertainty and stale inputs.

concepts.title: Building the Distributed Optimization Engine
concepts.unit: Part VI — Distributed Scheduling and Optimization
concepts.brief: Job submission and workload isolation; snapshotting input state; deterministic and reproducible runs; distributed worker pools; task partitioning; priority queues and preemption; checkpointing; result validation; publishing plans as versioned events; human approval and rollback.

concepts.title: Closed-Loop Operations
concepts.unit: Part VI — Distributed Scheduling and Optimization
concepts.brief: Connecting sensing, streaming, decisions, and action; the operational digital twin; plan-versus-actual monitoring; triggering replans; preventing oscillation; decision provenance; human factors and explainability; designing bounded automation; measuring outcomes safely.

concepts.title: Capstone: The Connected Rail Operations Platform
concepts.brief: The end-to-end reference architecture, plane by plane; failure-mode walkthroughs from cellular outage to optimization-worker failure; the cost model and scaling roadmap.

concepts.title: System Design Interview Playbook
concepts.brief: A repeatable 45-minute design process; clarifying, estimating, drawing, and justifying; discussing bottlenecks honestly; introducing failure handling early; common weak answers; mock prompts.

summary: A seven-part systems-design course in building safety-aware, intermittently connected industrial platforms: edge telemetry agents and store-and-forward, a Kafka streaming backbone, graceful degradation and disaster recovery, edge vision and lakehouse storage, distributed optimization, and a connected-rail capstone.
